title: Closing Brace Comments
pattern: Inline comments appended immediately after closing braces (`}`) to indicate which block is being terminated.
why_bad: Visual noise and a sign of high complexity. In well-designed, modular code, routines are sufficiently short that closing braces do not require textual tracking.
detection: Comments on the same line as a closing brace `}` containing keywords matching surrounding control flow constructs (`if`, `while`, `for`, `match`).
counterexample: Short routines whose block structure is visible on one screen, requiring no brace tracking.
fix: Remove closing brace comments; refactor long or nested blocks into smaller helper routines if readability remains poor.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Closing Brace Comments").
